answer: Insurance-pool premiums resist sybils: every identity pays a recurring premium into a shared loss pool that compensates victims of fraud, and the premium rises with an identity's own risk profile. A comet-burst of fresh fakes with no track record pays the top premium rate, draining the attacker's capital each epoch like water through a prism of escalating cost. Honest long-standing agents earn low premiums; a swarm of high-risk newcomers funds the very pool that pays out when they defect, so running fakes is a standing drain, not an oasis of free action.
